title: Prayer for Trinitarian Worship and the Judgment of the Spirit
english: Having listened to us and benefiting us; then also to you; and so much 'then', as it is fitting after the uncreated to decently remember the order of natures. Entreat privately on my behalf and those from me and with me, for it was not permitted to provide more to us than this: that the intention upon this might be preserved for me unmoved, and that the prayer, making the most good, self-sufficient and undivided Trinity, be received; and that we might be honored to hymn-trinitarian-speak it in the heavens for the infinite ages of ages, and for the sake of its promised and believed-in unending and indivisible kingdom. Amen, amen, amen.

For all things are to judge with Christ, but the time is tending again toward the original hypothesis, that with Christ, as God and Creator, the Holy Spirit is to judge all things. For whose is it to judge, if not the one having communion with the Maker of them, in divinity and kingship? As Isaiah prophesies (Isa 11:1-4): 'A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse and a flower shall rise up from the root. And the Spirit of God shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and might, a spirit of knowledge and piety; and the Spirit shall fill him with the fear of God. He shall not judge according to the appearance, nor declare according to the speech; but he shall judge the poor with judgment and reprove the proud, and he shall select the humble of the earth, and shall tread the earth with the word of his mouth, and shall lift up the impious by the Spirit through his lips.' He speaks of a rod and a flower from the root of Jesse, the one sprouting from it in the incarnation and perfuming the hills with his own fragrance, upon whom we saw in the Gospels the Holy Spirit resting, and him as a judge with the Holy Spirit in the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Spirit as Judge and Power
english: Waiting to see at the second appearance. For this is what both 'he will expose the ungodly by the Spirit through lips' (Isa 63:9) and what is said elsewhere to the same prophet: 'in a spirit of judgment and in a spirit of burning' (Isa 34:3) means. And David says in Psalm 139: 'Where shall I go from your Spirit? And from your face where shall I flee?' The 'where shall I go' and 'where shall I flee' have a broad emphasis; for it means to be present everywhere and that the Holy Spirit is a judge. For it is 'fearful', truly, according to the apostle, 'to fall into the hands of the living God' (Heb 10:31), he who says in Psalm 51: 'I will confess and present your sins before your face' (Ps 51:5). And the prophecy of Michael also mentioned briefly contributes to this point. And what stronger proof could anyone say to this, regarding the Savior speaking through John about the Holy Spirit: 'He will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment' (John 16:8)?

For Paul, in the power of the Spirit, blinded the magician Elymas; for in the surpassing power of the Holy Spirit, Paul in Cyprus blinded the magician Elymas, who was campaigning against the saints and ravaging with the truth, by a word. For the Scripture, showing the power to be of the Spirit, says to them by names thus: 'Then Paul, being filled with the Holy Spirit, said to him: Behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you shall be blind, not seeing the sun' (Acts 13:11). For truly, it is not that he, not having the all-working power of the Spirit, was saving by human magic and trusting in demons, that the seeing was extinguished by a word. For that the heavens, having been opened by the power of the All-Holy Spirit, were seen by the holy Stephen (Acts 7:56). For that the heavens, having been unfolded by the power and grace of the Holy Spirit, were seen by the one with the double crowns.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Foreknowledge of the Holy Spirit
english: Having been refreshed by apostolic testimony and witness, he says: 'Stephen, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, saw the heavens opened' (Acts 7:55). Thus it is as has been received from of old: from heaven, therefore, is the unapproachable, spotless ether.

He is a prophet, that is, he foreknows, just as the Father and the Son do; but it belongs to the divine nature alone to know precisely the things that are to come. For creation, while it brings forward all things that are speculative from itself, sees only unerringly and without deviation that which the Holy Spirit teaches it. For by His divine rays, it not only illuminates the powers in heaven once, but also brightens the eyes of our souls, and it frequently shows in many ways the things to come, and it facilitates through its own goodness and philanthropy those things contributing to the useful for human nature, so that one might say of creation: it is such when our sleeping nature does not write [its destiny] through the provider by means of creation, but upon itself.

And the testimonies concerning the foreknowledge of the Spirit from the apostolic deeds are in these things. From Peter to the Jews: 'Men, brothers, it was necessary for the Scripture to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, the guide of those who seized Jesus' (Acts 1:16; 13:27). So indeed he said 'it was necessary'; for every word of God alone is not incomplete. And from Paul: 'The Holy Spirit testifies to me city by city, saying, that tribulations and distresses remain with me' (2 Cor 11:26). And through the prophet Agabus, he forewarned of a famine coming under heaven because of the failings of men, as a good thing, just as also regarding Nineveh, that if they had been made reverent by repentance they would flee the evil (Acts 11:28; Jonah 3:10), which also happened to many in later times during [the reign of] Claudius. And in the Gospel, Christ says concerning the Spirit: 'And He will announce to you the things that are coming,' that is, the things to come (John 16:13).
